_readme: Electrical steel grades offered. Edit the text values freely; keep the keys. Shown on the home page, /materials and each product page. "facts" are the short bullet points under the specification table on /materials.

materials.name: Cold-Rolled Grain-Oriented electrical steel
materials.grades: 70 to 120 grade, depending on material specification and availability
materials.summary: Primarily used in transformer cores because its directional magnetic properties make it suitable for efficient magnetic flux conduction.
materials.detail: Proper material selection and precision processing are important for achieving the required core performance.
facts: Its grains run along the rolling direction, so flux flows best along the length of the strip. Core corners are mitred at 45° to keep the flux close to the grain at the joints.
Step-lap stacking staggers the joints in small steps, so the flux crosses them gradually. This lowers core loss and transformer noise.
Each sheet carries a thin insulating coating that limits eddy currents. Cutting burrs can bridge that coating, so clean edges matter.

materials.name: Cold-Rolled Non-Grain-Oriented electrical steel
materials.grades: 230 to 360 grade in 0.35 mm; 350 to 1000 grade in 0.50 mm
materials.summary: Uniform magnetic properties in all directions. Used for E&I laminations in small transformers and chokes.
materials.detail: Grade is selected to match the core loss the design requires.
facts: Its magnetic properties are the same in every direction, which suits the changing flux path in E&I cores. It is also the standard steel for electric motors for the same reason.
Many standard E&I sizes are scrapless: the I is punched from the window of the E, so very little steel is wasted.
Thinner sheet has lower eddy-current loss, so 0.35 mm loses less energy than 0.50 mm.
